name: Checkout With An Unrefunded Credit
natural_language: A reservation cannot be closed while the hotel still owes the guest a refund.

population.description: Reservations that reached checked-out status in the last 24 hours. Bounding this set matters: the folio endpoint is one call per reservation.

then: GetReservationBalance once per reservation in the population
minihotel.call_cost: 1 + N where N is checkouts in the window, NOT total reservations - this is why the population query exists (R1)

predicates.note: A negative balance means the guest overpaid and is owed a refund. Observed live: reservation 007004348 departed at -490.75 ILS.

required_evidence.note: needed only to detect the currency split; the comparison itself is against 0 so no FX is required

execution.rationale: Type D in control_rule_architecture.docx section 8 - inherently a review queue rather than a real-time alert. Lower urgency than money owed, which is exactly why the two controls were separated (D8).

freshness_requirement.rationale: A credit owed to a departed guest is a liability to settle, not a debt to chase before they leave the country. Daily is enough.

unknown_conditions.when: the GetReservationBalance call fails or returns no folio
any rule variant compares folio.balance_due against reservation.total_amount
unknown_conditions.reason: folio.currency and reservation.currency differ (ILS vs USD observed live) and MiniHotel supplies no exchange rate. Comparing them without an FX source is invalid.

caveats: Asserts against literal zero, so it is currency-safe by construction (R9).

Question 2.2 for MiniHotel is open: we infer that a negative TotalDebit is an overpayment. If the vendor says it is an accounting artefact instead, this control is wrong and should be withdrawn rather than reinterpreted.
